category_title: Struggling readers who ask relevant questions to discontinue reading
scenario_title: Shared reading of 'Where the wild things are'
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are doing a shared reading of 'Where the wild things are', and it is the student's turn to read from the new text.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the next page of 'Where the wild things are'. It is your turn to read.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's look at the next page of 'Where the wild things are'. It is your turn to read.

STUDENT: (Switches gaze directly to the text)

TUTOR: Go ahead and start.

STUDENT: stepped into his private...

TUTOR: What is the next word?

STUDENT: Why's it private?

task.content: Initiating a reading turn from new text during shared reading sessions.

context.materials: Where the wild things are (book selected from several choices)

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: After a reading attempt of four words, ‘stepped into his private. . .'
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Before reading very far, even before attaching a noun to the descriptor, he shifts the interactive turn back to the interventionist by asking, ‘Why ’s it private?'

behavior_patterns.condition: within the first five words read
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: nonverbally assents to read by switching gaze more directly to the text followed by a reading attempt... avoided reading more by asking the interventionist a question relevant to the story itself or about a particular word
behavior_patterns.internal_state: strategically avoidant rather than sincere inquiries
